subject: economics
title: Comparative Advantage
welcome_lead: Ricardo's classic case for specialisation and trade.
meta_desc: A-Level Trade: comparative advantage and terms of trade.
final_note: Trade lets countries gain from differences in opportunity cost.

concepts.def: Producing a good using fewer resources.
Lower opportunity cost in a good.
Value of the next best alternative given up.
Ratio of export prices to import prices.
Focusing production on goods of comparative advantage.
Both countries can gain from trade with comparative advantage.

walkthroughs.body_html: Even if one country can produce everything more cheaply, trade still pays - both gain when each specialises in its comparative advantage and trades.
Terms of trade = export prices / import prices x 100. A rise (improvement) means each unit of exports buys more imports. Commodity shocks swing developing economies sharply.
Comparative advantage assumes fixed factors, no transport cost and full employment. In reality, jobs lost to imports may not be quickly replaced - losers need support.

options: Imports get cheaper relative to exports
Trade balance moves to surplus automatically
